name: אֱלִיצָפָן
gloss: My God has hidden; or my God has treasured
summary: Borne by Elizaphan (Elzaphan) son of Uzziel, Aaron's cousin, who with Mishael carried the bodies of Nadab and Abihu out of the camp (Lev 10:4) and was chief of the Kohathite clans (Num 3:30), whose sons served under David and Hezekiah (1Ch 15:8; 2Ch 29:13); and by Elizaphan son of Parnach, the leader of Zebulun chosen to divide the land (Num 34:25). The name is אֵלִי “my God” with the qal of צָפַן, “has hidden” or “has treasured”, the verb of Psa 27:5, “he will hide me in his shelter”. Scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “The chief of the father's house of the Kohathite clans was אֱלִיצָפָן son of Uzziel.”
“The sons of Uzziel: Mishael, אֶלְצָפָן and Sithri.”
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan to carry their brothers out of the camp.
“For the tribe of the sons of Zebulun a leader, אֱלִיצָפָן son of Parnach.”
“He will hide me (יִצְפְּנֵנִי) in his shelter in the day of trouble”: the verb of the name.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. BDB files the name under אלה: a.dl.ba אֱלִיצָפָן and a.dl.bv אֶלְצָפָן (the short spelling of Exo 6:22; Lev 10:4). TIPNR names Elizaphan son of Uzziel by the key Elizaphan@Exo.6.22.
